title: Every portal lead answered in under a minute
metaDescription: Example project: a 12-agent Texas brokerage replies to every property portal lead by text in under a minute, then books the viewing on the right calendar.
duration: 8 weeks from audit to full rollout
summary: Portal enquiries used to wait hours for a reply on evenings and weekends. Now each one gets a text within a minute, three qualifying questions, and a viewing slot on the right agent's calendar.

results.label: First reply to a new lead

problem: Most enquiries arrived from two property portals and the brokerage's own website, and most of them arrived after 6pm. Whoever was on rota copied each one into the CRM by hand and called back when they could.
On a weekday that meant a reply within the hour. On a Saturday it could mean Monday. By then the buyer had usually spoken to another agent.
The owner did not want more software for agents to log in to. She wanted every lead answered quickly, and her agents talking only to people who were ready to view.

paragraphs: We started with one portal and one agent for three weeks. Once the replies read the way the team would write them, we added the second portal, the website form and the rest of the agents.

The assistant only does the first five minutes. It replies, asks about budget, area and timing, and offers viewing times from the agent's real calendar. A person takes over from there, with a short summary waiting in the CRM.

automations.name: Instant lead reply
automations.what: A text goes out within a minute of the enquiry, naming the property the buyer asked about.

automations.name: Qualifying questions
automations.what: Budget, preferred area and move date, asked one at a time in plain language.

automations.name: Viewing booking
automations.what: Free slots are read from the agent's calendar, and the booking is confirmed to both sides.

automations.name: Handover summary
automations.what: The CRM record is created with the answers and a three-line summary, so the agent never starts cold.

automations.name: Quiet-lead nudge
automations.what: If a buyer goes silent, one polite follow-up is sent the next morning, then the lead is passed to a person.

flow.title: What happens when a lead arrives

timeline.what: Followed 40 recent leads from enquiry to first call, and timed every gap along the way.
One portal, one agent. Every reply was reviewed daily and the wording adjusted with the team.
Second portal, website form, all 12 calendars, the CRM handover and the morning nudge.
Reply wording reviewed each month, new listings and agents added, and a one-page report for the owner.

title: A receptionist that answers every call and WhatsApp message
metaDescription: Example project: a four-chair Manchester dental practice has calls and WhatsApp messages answered day and night, with reminders that reduce missed appointments.
duration: 9 weeks from audit to full rollout
summary: The front desk could not answer the phone and look after the patient in front of them at the same time. An AI receptionist now picks up every call and WhatsApp message, books routine visits, and passes anything urgent to a person.
problem: The phone rang most during the morning rush, exactly when the front desk was checking patients in. Calls that went to voicemail were rarely returned the same day.
Patients also messaged the practice on WhatsApp, where replies depended on who had the practice phone that afternoon.
Reminders were sent by hand on quiet days and skipped on busy ones, so missed appointments rose in the busiest weeks.

paragraphs: The receptionist answers on the practice's existing number and WhatsApp line. It books, moves and cancels routine appointments in the practice diary, and answers the common questions about opening hours, parking and prices.
It never gives clinical advice. Anyone describing pain, swelling or bleeding is passed straight to a member of staff during hours, and given the emergency line out of hours.
We piloted on WhatsApp alone for three weeks before switching on the phone line, so the team could read every conversation and correct the wording.

automations.name: Call and message answering
automations.what: Every call and WhatsApp message is answered, day and night, in the practice's own tone.

automations.name: Appointment booking
automations.what: Check-ups and hygiene visits are booked, moved or cancelled directly in the diary.

automations.name: Appointment reminders

automations.name: Patient recall

automations.name: Urgent handover
automations.what: Pain or swelling is flagged to the front desk at once, with the patient's own words attached.

timeline.what: Counted calls, voicemails and missed appointments for a month, and listed the 20 questions patients ask most.
WhatsApp only, routine bookings only. Front desk read every conversation at the end of each day.
Phone line, reminders, recall messages and the urgent handover, tested with staff acting as patients.
Conversation review, price and hours updates, and a monthly count of calls, bookings and handovers.

title: Call notes, CRM updates and follow-ups, written for the rep
metaDescription: Example project: a nine-person Sydney B2B sales team gets call notes, CRM updates and follow-up drafts written within minutes of every customer meeting.
clientType: 9-person B2B sales team at a software reseller, Sydney
duration: 7 weeks from audit to full rollout
summary: Reps were writing up calls at night or not at all, so the CRM was out of date and follow-ups slipped. Now the notes, the CRM fields and a draft follow-up are ready within minutes of the call ending.

results.label: Follow-up draft ready
results.note: After the call ends. Was next day

results.label: Calls with notes in the CRM
Deals with a next step logged

problem: Each rep ran four to six customer calls a day. Notes lived in notebooks, in personal documents, or in the rep's head.
The sales manager could not trust the pipeline report, because half the deals had no recent notes and no next step.
Follow-up emails went out the next day at best. Customers who had been keen on the call had cooled by the time the summary arrived.

paragraphs: Calls are recorded with the customer's consent, transcribed, and turned into a short structured note: what was discussed, objections, budget, who decides, and the agreed next step.

The note is filed against the right deal in the CRM and the deal fields are updated. A follow-up email is drafted in the rep's own style and left in their drafts folder. Nothing is sent to a customer without the rep reading it first.

automations.what: A one-page summary of each call, in the same five headings every time.

title: Invoices matched to bank lines, with only the exceptions left
metaDescription: Example project: an eight-person Dubai bookkeeping firm has supplier invoices read and matched to bank lines automatically, leaving people only the exceptions.
duration: 10 weeks from audit to full rollout
summary: Bookkeepers spent the first week of every month keying in supplier invoices and ticking them off against bank statements. Now invoices are read and matched automatically, and people only see the ones that do not add up.
problem: The firm looked after the books of about 45 small businesses. Supplier invoices arrived as email attachments, phone photos and the occasional scan.
Each one was typed into the accounting software, then matched by eye to a line on the bank statement. It was careful work, and nearly all of it was routine.
The partners wanted month-end done faster without hiring, and they wanted a person to check anything unusual rather than everything.

paragraphs: The audit showed that four in five invoices were plain: one supplier, one amount, one matching bank line. Those are now read, coded and matched without anyone touching them.

Anything else goes to an exceptions queue with the reason spelled out: amount differs, possible duplicate, supplier not recognised, or VAT number missing. A bookkeeper decides, and the rule is updated if the same case keeps appearing.
Every automatic match keeps a link to the original document, so a partner can check any entry in two clicks.

automations.name: Invoice capture
automations.what: Attachments and photos sent to one inbox are read and turned into supplier, date, amount and VAT.

automations.name: Bank line matching
automations.what: Each invoice is matched to its payment by amount, date and supplier reference.

automations.name: Exceptions queue
automations.what: Anything that does not match cleanly is listed with the reason and a suggested fix.

automations.name: Missing document chaser
automations.what: Clients get a weekly message listing payments that still have no invoice.

flow.title: What happens to a supplier invoice

Five clients, one bookkeeper. Every automatic match was double-checked by hand for a full month-end.
All 45 clients, the exceptions queue, the document chaser and the partner spot-check view.
Matching rules tuned from the exceptions, new suppliers added, and a monthly accuracy sample for the partners.
